maxMintPerDay.semantics: Rolling 24h window per stablecoin, denominated in phUSD (18dp). 0 disables. Window resets when block.timestamp >= lastMintTimestamp + 1 days (:216), which also covers the first-ever mint since lastMintTimestamp starts at 0.
maxMintPerDay.windowShape: Not a sliding window — it is a hard 24h epoch that only advances when a mint occurs after expiry, so a mint at t and another at t+1day-1s both charge the same window while a mint at t+1day starts a fresh full allowance. Standard behaviour for this pattern.
maxMintPerDay.criticalNote: This cap is charged ONLY for phUSD the minter itself mints. Antimatter's second leg (Antimatter.sol:236) is minted directly on Antimatter's own FlaxToken authorisation and never touches this counter — see AM-LOCAL-002.

observationsRelevantToAntimatter: registerStablecoin (:111) OVERWRITES the whole struct, resetting maxMintPerDay/mintedToday/lastMintTimestamp to 0 (:120-128). Re-registering an existing stable (e.g. to change its yield strategy) therefore silently deletes its daily cap and clears the current window. Owner footgun; belongs to the minter's own audit, noted here because it removes a rail that bounds annihilation volume.

registerStablecoin does NOT validate `decimals` against IERC20Metadata(stablecoin).decimals(). A mis-entered decimals value propagates straight into Antimatter's pairing ratio (Antimatter.sol:254) AND into the mint formula (:254), in the same direction — a stable registered with 6 decimals when it really has 18 would make Antimatter pull 1e-12 of the intended stablecoin while still minting the full phUSD. Antimatter has no independent decimals check to catch this. Cross-contract; flagged for interaction analysis.

registerStablecoin does not require approveYS, and approveYS is a separate owner call (:180). A registered-but-unapproved stable passes Antimatter's registration check (Antimatter.sol:251) and then reverts inside :229. Liveness footgun.
updateExchangeRate (:138) has no bound, no timelock and no upper/lower sanity check.
mint() is permissionless, so Antimatter is not privileged on the minter — it is just another caller.
